messages.author: c4391c6727fe6d94
messages.subject: Error running secr.fit
parts:
Hi all,


I am having trouble running the secr.fit() function. I am able to compile the capture history object, but every time I run the secr.fit() function, I get the following message:

Error in 1:nrow(xy) : argument of length 0

Here's some context: 
1) I have 18 spatial sessions. 
2) Each session consists of only 1 polygon. 
3) Of the 18 sessions, 10 sessions do not have any captures.

Here is my code:
edf <- read.table("c_capt_n.txt", header=T)

tdf1 <- read.traps(file="sessA.txt", detector="polygon", trapID="Detector")
tdf2 <- read.traps(file="sessB.txt", detector="polygon", trapID="Detector")
tdf3 <- read.traps(file="sessC.txt", detector="polygon", trapID="Detector")
tdf4 <- read.traps(file="sessD_2.txt", detector="polygon", trapID="Detector")
tdf5 <- read.traps(file="sessE.txt", detector="polygon", trapID="Detector")
tdf6 <- read.traps(file="sessF_2.txt", detector="polygon", trapID="Detector")
tdf7 <- read.traps(file="sessG_2.txt", detector="polygon", trapID="Detector")
tdf8 <- read.traps(file="sessH_2.txt", detector="polygon", trapID="Detector")
tdf9 <- read.traps(file="sessI.txt", detector="polygon", trapID="Detector")
tdf10 <- read.traps(file="sessJ_2.txt", detector="polygon", trapID="Detector")
tdf11 <- read.traps(file="sessK.txt", detector="polygon", trapID="Detector")
tdf12 <- read.traps(file="sessL_2.txt", detector="polygon", trapID="Detector")
tdf13 <- read.traps(file="sessM.txt", detector="polygon", trapID="Detector")
tdf14 <- read.traps(file="sessN.txt", detector="polygon", trapID="Detector")
tdf15 <- read.traps(file="sessO.txt", detector="polygon", trapID="Detector")
tdf16 <- read.traps(file="sessP_2.txt", detector="polygon", trapID="Detector")
tdf17 <- read.traps(file="sessQ.txt", detector="polygon", trapID="Detector")
tdf18 <- read.traps(file="sessR.txt", detector="polygon", trapID="Detector")


catCH <- make.capthist(captures=edf, traps=list(tdf1,tdf2,tdf3,tdf4,tdf5,tdf6,tdf7,tdf8,tdf9,tdf10,tdf11,tdf12,tdf13,tdf14,tdf15,tdf16,tdf17,tdf18), fmt="XY", noccasions=4, noncapt="NONE")

catmasks <- make.mask(traps(catCH), buffer=500, type='trapbuffer')

m1 <- secr.fit(catCH, mask=catmasks, model=list(D~session, lambda0~1, sigma~1))

I have attached the data files and would appreciate any help or advice you can offer.


Cheers,
Josh

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Error running secr.fit
parts:
Hi Josh
That error comes from verify() and can be avoided by setting verify=FALSE in the call to secr.fit. Then you will encounter a problem with initial values (because the first session has no captures from which to infer the detection scale). You can get around that by including details = list(autoini = 14). Then it's just very slow... You don't need to be told this, but the data are rather thin as there are only 3 recaptures at more than 20 metres. I wouldn't bother with session-specific densities, and I would be looking to speed up fitting by tuning the masks (reduce buffer <=250 m, set spacing, say 15 m?) and perhaps discretizing the polygons (but that doesn't work with empty sessions in the current version).
Murray

messages.subject: Re: Error running secr.fit
parts:
Hi Murray,

I tried running the model on multiple different computers, but it all failed.

Eventually, I excluded the empty sessions, and the model finally ran! (without the need for verify=F or autoini=14)
However, I found that the models could take a very long time to complete (one model took 38h to complete). Therefore, I discretized the capture history and tried analyzing it with secr.fit().

tdf1 <- read.traps(file="sessN.txt", detector="polygon", trapID="Detector")
tdf2 <- read.traps(file="sessO.txt", detector="polygon", trapID="Detector")
tdf3 <- read.traps(file="sessP_2.txt", detector="polygon", trapID="Detector")
tdf4 <- read.traps(file="sessQ.txt", detector="polygon", trapID="Detector")
tdf5 <- read.traps(file="sessR.txt", detector="polygon", trapID="Detector")


catCH <- make.capthist(captures=edf, traps=list(tdf1,tdf2,tdf3,tdf4,tdf5), fmt="XY", noccasions=4)

discreteCH <- discretize(catCH, spacing=10, output='count')
discretemask <- make.mask(traps(discreteCH), buffer=500, type='trapbuffer')

m9 <- secr.fit(discreteCH, mask=discretemask, model=list(D~session, lambda0~1, sigma~1), verify=FALSE)

Unfortunately, I ran into this error:

Error in secr.fit(discreteCH, mask = discretemask, model = list(D ~ session,  :
  parameters in model not consistent with detectfn etc. : lambda0

Any idea where I went wrong?


Cheers,
Josh

On Friday, December 31, 2021 at 4:17:06 AM UTC+8 murray...@gmail.com wrote:
Hi Josh
That error comes from verify() and can be avoided by setting verify=FALSE in the call to secr.fit. Then you will encounter a problem with initial values (because the first session has no captures from which to infer the detection scale). You can get around that by including details = list(autoini = 14). Then it's just very slow... You don't need to be told this, but the data are rather thin as there are only 3 recaptures at more than 20 metres. I wouldn't bother with session-specific densities, and I would be looking to speed up fitting by tuning the masks (reduce buffer <=250 m, set spacing, say 15 m?) and perhaps discretizing the polygons (but that doesn't work with empty sessions in the current version).
Murray
